reason: This passage (Exodus 3) describes God's commissioning of Moses to lead Israel out of Egypt. The text emphasizes God's compassion for the suffering of the people ('I have surely seen the affliction of my people... and have heard their cry'), divine rescue and deliverance, and God's promise of presence and support. While violence is mentioned—God's plagues against Egypt (וְהִכֵּיתִי אֶת־ מִצְרַיִם)—this is directed at an external oppressor, not at 'unruly people' within the group being led. The leadership model presented focuses on empathy, listening to the oppressed, divine authority, and deliverance from oppression, not on violence toward unruly members of one's own people.
